key_insight: Visual Attribution Distillation (VAD) focuses on identifying which student corrections are actually grounded in visual evidence, instead of treating all teacher corrections as equally useful. This makes multimodal distillation more precise by separating true visual supervision from language priors and teacher-specific noise.
problem_solved: Multimodal on-policy distillation (OPD) transfers knowledge using teacher corrections on student-generated outputs, but those corrections are source-mixed: they blend visual cues, linguistic priors, and teacher idiosyncrasies. The paper addresses the challenge of attributing corrections to visual evidence so distillation targets only the parts that truly come from the image.
method: Uses a counterfactual target-reconstruction framework to estimate whether a correction is supported by visual evidence.
Filters or weights distillation signals based on visual attribution rather than raw next-token disagreement.
Targets fine-grained visual knowledge transfer while reducing contamination from non-visual signals.
impact: For practitioners, VAD offers a cleaner way to distill multimodal models so students learn from the image, not just from teacher quirks or language shortcuts. This can improve training efficiency, robustness, and faithfulness in vision-language systems.
visual_elements: A side-by-side pipeline showing standard OPD vs. VAD with 'mixed signals' vs. 'visual attribution' paths.

paper_title: VAD: Attributing Visual Evidence for Target Reconstruction in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
paper_authors: Kangning Zhang, Yixing Li, Shuai Shao, Qingyao Li, Zhengxi Lu
